title: Markets: Thursday 5 November

morning.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · before the 10:00 open
summary: Democrats won both houses of Congress, and Wall Street rallied on its first full session after the result: the S&P 500 rose 1.72% and the Dow 2.97%, while chip, data-centre and defence stocks fell ([Reuters via StreetInsider](https://www.streetinsider.com/General+News/Wall+Street+rallies+after+Democrats+win+Congress%3B+data+center+stocks+slide/27284408.html)). Brent settled 8.7% lower at US$94.62 after Trump said he had no immediate plans to strike Iran again ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/oil-price-iran-war-us-election-strait-hormuz.html)).

S&P/ASX 200 futures rose 173 points (2.0%) to 9,029 near 6am AEDT ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-wall-street-rallies-oil-falls-below-us100-20261105-p61bir)), after the index fell 0.6% to 8,834.5 on Wednesday (snapshot). Cheaper oil lowers fuel costs but weighs on energy producers, and gold futures rose 3.4% (snapshot).

NAB reports its full-year result today and ABS trade data is due at 11:30am. The Bank of England is expected to raise rates to 4% at 11pm AEDT ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/bank-of-england-poised-to-raise-rates-but-may-push-back-on-bets-for-more-4989788)), and US payrolls follow at 12:30am Saturday.

cards.headline: Democrats win both houses of Congress; the Dow jumps 3% and the S&P 500 1.7%
cards.takeaway: Wall Street rallied on its first session after the midterms, led by consumer stocks, healthcare and the biggest tech names, while energy fell 5.1%.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Yesterday covered the count as it began. New: Democrats won the Senate as well as the House, and this is the full US session after the result.
cards.what_happened: The S&P 500 rose 1.72% to 7,698.86, the Nasdaq 1.77% to 25,821.13 and the Dow 2.97% (1,534.89 points) to 53,321.61 on Wednesday, according to Reuters. Consumer discretionary rose 5% and energy fell 5.1% ([Reuters via StreetInsider](https://www.streetinsider.com/General+News/Wall+Street+rallies+after+Democrats+win+Congress%3B+data+center+stocks+slide/27284408.html)). The Fox News Decision Desk projected Democrats would take the House ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/democrat-seize-house-control-stunning-blue-tsunami-vow-retribution-against-trump-admin)), and Democrats also won the Senate ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/treasury-yields-fall-as-democrats-win-big-in-us-midterm-elections.html)). The S&P 500 was heading for its best day since April, according to AP ([AP](https://apnews.com/article/stock-markets-ai-earnings-oil-4d12764c0b3ce38ffde3077712811182)).
cards.why_it_matters: The result could make it harder for the White House to push legislation through Congress, and Treasuries rallied as traders focused on reduced deficit spending ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/treasury-yields-fall-as-democrats-win-big-in-us-midterm-elections.html)). Healthcare and clean energy rose, while defence and AI-infrastructure names fell ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/every-stock-thats-moving-as-a-result-of-the-election.html)). That sector split matters for the ASX, where materials and data-centre-linked stocks fell on Wednesday ahead of the US session.
cards.market_reaction: Apple and Microsoft rose more than 6%, with Apple touching a record high, while Alphabet gained 4% and Meta 3% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/every-stock-thats-moving-as-a-result-of-the-election.html)). The snapshot still shows Tuesday's US closes because Wednesday's session ended after the cutoff.
cards.what_to_watch: US payrolls at 12:30am Saturday Sydney time, and whether Congress and the White House agree on government funding.

competing_views.who: Terry Sandven, U.S. Bank Wealth Management
competing_views.view: Said the result "introduces a degree of gridlock to the economic backdrop and that oftentimes is favorable for equity prices".
Said Wall Street is focusing on "reduced deficit spending", which could come through budget fights and "likely wading through a government shutdown".

cards.headline: Brent falls 8.7% to US$94.62, its first settle below US$100 since early October
cards.takeaway: Oil fell as analysts said the election result gives Trump more reason to make a deal with Iran, after he said he had no immediate plans to strike Iran again.
cards.key_figure: Brent futures US$95.34, −8.0% at 7.22am AEDT (snapshot); settled US$94.62, −8.7% (CNBC)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Yesterday Brent settled at US$103.60 after a US$6 range. New: the biggest one-day fall of the week, and the first move below US$100 since early October.
cards.what_happened: Brent futures settled 8.7% lower at US$94.62 a barrel and WTI fell 8.3% to US$88.12 ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/oil-price-iran-war-us-election-strait-hormuz.html)). Brent had fallen below US$100 for the first time since early October during the London session ([Reuters via Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/commodities/brent-crude-drops-below-100-for-first-time-since-october-as-investors-assess-post-election-iran-war-outlook-14070367.html)). Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday that he had no immediate plans to strike Iran, and Vice President JD Vance posted that "the reason we lost is the war" ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/oil-price-iran-war-us-election-strait-hormuz.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Oil futures have fallen more than 14% this week, according to CNBC. A sustained fall would lower fuel costs, which are part of the consumer price index the RBA targets, but it cuts into the revenue outlook for Woodside and Santos.
cards.market_reaction: Brent futures US$95.34, −8.0%, at 7.22am AEDT (snapshot). US energy stocks fell 5.1% (Reuters).
cards.what_to_watch: Any statement from Washington or Tehran on talks, and weekly US inventory data.

competing_views.view: Said the sell-off "could be getting a bit overdone", with the market in "shoot first, ask questions later" mode.
Said the odds still favour military escalation because Iran is "hardened in its uncompromising position" and Trump is unlikely to give up his goal of preventing an Iranian nuclear weapon.

cards.headline: Chip, data-centre and defence stocks fall while the wider market rallies
cards.takeaway: The Philadelphia semiconductor index hit a six-month low as investors weighed tighter data-centre and AI scrutiny under a Democratic Congress.
cards.key_figure: Philadelphia semiconductor index at a six-month low, 4 Nov (Reuters)
cards.what_happened: Democrats made gains in data-centre states including Texas and Georgia, where public opposition to the industry's expansion has been growing. Data-centre operators IREN and Hut 8 fell sharply, and AMD fell even after forecasting faster-than-expected growth in 2027. Defence stocks fell because Trump's US$1.5 trillion defence budget request could face a tougher Congress, while the Invesco Solar ETF climbed sharply ([Reuters via StreetInsider](https://www.streetinsider.com/General+News/Wall+Street+rallies+after+Democrats+win+Congress%3B+data+center+stocks+slide/27284408.html)). CoreWeave fell 9% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/every-stock-thats-moving-as-a-result-of-the-election.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: The same theme drove the ASX lower on Wednesday: Market Index linked the 1.5% fall in materials to fears about AI spending and data-centre regulation, since copper is used heavily in both. Australian defence names EOS (−7.8%) and DroneShield (−7.6%) were among the worst performers ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/evening-wrap-asx-200-sags-as-mining-sell-off-intensifies-us-election-results)).

competing_views.view: Said "the AI trade will face some headwinds", because a slower data-centre build-out changes "the fundamental trajectory for many of those suppliers".

cards.what_to_watch: Whether copper holds near US$6.35/lb, which Market Index flagged as technical support, and how NextDC and Goodman trade today.

cards.headline: Gold futures rise 3.4% back above US$4,000 as the US dollar slips
cards.takeaway: Precious metals rallied as Treasury yields and the US dollar fell after the election.
cards.what_happened: Spot gold rose 3.4% to US$4,061.30 an ounce and spot silver 5.1% to US$52.29, while the US dollar index fell about 0.3% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/gold-silver-platinum-dollar-midterms.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Gold is still down more than 6% this year as high inflation and hawkish central banks have weighed on it, according to CNBC. A weaker US dollar usually supports the Australian dollar, which was at US$0.6972 at the RBA's 4pm fix on Wednesday (snapshot).
cards.what_to_watch: US payrolls on Saturday morning Sydney time, which will shape bets on a December Fed hike.

competing_views.view: Said Democratic control of Congress should support gold as rates and the dollar come under pressure, though "the Iran war and a weaker dollar would compete with [the] impact of [a] hawkish Fed".
Said the recovery "remains fragile" because geopolitical risk is not translating into safe-haven demand while monetary policy stays restrictive.

cards.headline: ASX 200 futures point to a 2% rise after Wednesday's 0.6% fall
cards.takeaway: Futures were up 173 points to 9,029 near 6am AEDT, which would more than reverse Wednesday's defensive sell-off.
cards.key_figure: ASX 200 futures +173 points (2.0%) to 9,029 near 6am AEDT (AFR); ASX 200 closed 8,834.5, −0.6%, on 4 Nov (snapshot)
cards.new_since_last_issue: The close edition reported Wednesday's fall. New: the overnight futures move after Wall Street's rally.
cards.what_happened: S&P/ASX 200 futures rose 173 points, or 2.0%, to 9,029 near 6am AEDT ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/markets/equity-markets/asx-to-rise-wall-street-rallies-oil-falls-below-us100-20261105-p61bir)). On Wednesday the index fell 0.6% to 8,834.5 (snapshot). Utilities (+1.2%) and energy (+0.9%) rose, while materials (−1.5%) and industrials (−1.3%) fell ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/evening-wrap-asx-200-sags-as-mining-sell-off-intensifies-us-election-results)).
cards.why_it_matters: Wednesday's fall happened while US futures were sliding on the early count. Wall Street's full-session rally leaves local investors weighing a broad risk-on move against the 8.7% drop in oil, which hurts energy producers.
cards.what_to_watch: NAB's full-year result today, Amcor's first-quarter result around the open, Woodside's investor day, and ABS trade data at 11:30am.

cards.headline: Oil's fall and gold's jump pull ASX resources in opposite directions
cards.takeaway: ASX energy stocks rose and gold miners fell on Wednesday, before oil fell 8.7% and gold rose 3.4% overnight.
cards.what_happened: On Wednesday, Woodside and Santos each rose 1.0% and Viva Energy 4.1%, while the gold sub-index fell 0.8% even as COMEX gold rose in Asian trade, according to Market Index ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/evening-wrap-asx-200-sags-as-mining-sell-off-intensifies-us-election-results)). Overnight, Brent settled 8.7% lower ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/oil-price-iran-war-us-election-strait-hormuz.html)) and gold futures rose 3.4% (snapshot).
cards.why_it_matters: Both of Wednesday's sector moves ran against the direction of the overnight commodity prices, so energy producers and gold miners face the largest swing in inputs at the open.
cards.market_reaction: Brent futures US$95.34, −8.0%; gold futures US$4,072.9, +3.4% (snapshot).
cards.what_to_watch: Woodside's investor day today, for any change to its production or spending plans after oil's fall.

cards.headline: US 10-year yield falls about 5bp to 4.90% on expectations of tighter spending
cards.takeaway: Treasuries rallied across the curve as investors expect a divided Congress to limit deficit spending.
cards.what_happened: The 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 5bp to 4.898%, the 2-year more than 4bp to 4.573% and the 30-year more than 3bp to 5.293% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/treasury-yields-fall-as-democrats-win-big-in-us-midterm-elections.html)). Australian 10-year yields had already fallen 5bp to 5.05% during Wednesday's session ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-wednesday-4th-november)).
cards.why_it_matters: Lower US long yields can flow through to Australian bond yields, which matter for rate-sensitive sectors such as property trusts, which fell 1.1% on Wednesday.
cards.what_to_watch: US payrolls at 12:30am Saturday Sydney time.

competing_views.view: Said a divided policy environment "should make deficit growth more difficult and potentially improve the fiscal outlook".
Said lower long yields could be "offset by debt-limit premia in bills and a Fed leaning towards another hike".

cards.headline: US services activity eases slightly while ADP shows 86,000 new private jobs
cards.takeaway: The ISM services index dipped to 54.5, a little below the Reuters poll, while its prices index stayed high at 73.0.
cards.key_figure: ISM services 54.5 in October vs 54.9 in September; Reuters poll 54.8
cards.what_happened: The ISM services index fell to 54.5 in October from 54.9, below the 54.8 forecast by economists polled by Reuters. New orders fell to 55.9 from 59.8, prices paid eased to 73.0 from 74.0, and employment rose to 51.4 from 50.1 ([ISM](https://www.ismworld.org/supply-management-news-and-reports/reports/ism-pmi-reports/services/october/); [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-services-sector-activity-cools-slightly-in-october-inflation-remains-elevated-5000201)). ADP reported 86,000 private jobs added in October ([ADP](https://adpemploymentreport.com/)).
cards.why_it_matters: Prices paid near 73 keep inflation pressure in view for the Fed, which left rates at 3.75%–4.00% last week. Economists expect the Fed to raise rates in December, according to Reuters.
cards.what_to_watch: October payrolls at 12:30am Saturday Sydney time; the Reuters poll expects 65,000 jobs and an unchanged 4.2% unemployment rate.

cards.headline: Bank of England expected to raise rates to 4% tonight, its first rise since August 2023
cards.takeaway: Economists polled by Reuters expect a 25bp rise to 4.0% at 11pm AEDT, on a 7–2 vote.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Previously listed only in the calendar. New: the decision is tonight.
cards.what_happened: Economists polled by Reuters expect the Bank of England to raise Bank Rate to 4.0% from 3.75%, with external members Alan Taylor and Swati Dhingra the most likely to vote to hold. UK inflation was 3.5% in the year to September, above the Bank's July forecast of 3.0% ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/bank-of-england-poised-to-raise-rates-but-may-push-back-on-bets-for-more-4989788)).
cards.why_it_matters: The Fed and the ECB raised rates before the BoE in this energy shock ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/bank-of-england-poised-to-raise-rates-but-may-push-back-on-bets-for-more-4989788)). A BoE rise would add to tightening by major central banks, the same backdrop the RBA faces.
cards.what_to_watch: The decision at 11pm AEDT and the press conference with Governor Andrew Bailey at 11.30pm.

competing_views.view: Said the Bank's "hands are increasingly being forced" and it has to deliver some of what markets price.
Said the Bank may signal that Bank Rate is unlikely to reach the 4.75%–5.0% priced by markets for 2027.

cards.headline: Trump says the Iran war was part of the loss; Iran says US voters rejected the war
cards.takeaway: Trump said the war was "a piece of" the Republicans' defeat but that he did the right thing, while Iran's parliament speaker welcomed the result.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Yesterday covered Trump's cut to Israel aid. New: Trump's and Vance's comments on the war after the result, and Iran's response.
cards.what_happened: Trump said "Iran was a piece of it… I did the right thing" ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/politics-news/trump-acknowledges-iran-played-role-in-republican-midterm-losses-4997350)), and that "if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again, because long term, it's the only answer" ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-couldnt-transfer-love-supporters-other-republicans-amid-historic-midterm-loss)). Vance posted that "the reason we lost is the war" ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/oil-price-iran-war-us-election-strait-hormuz.html)). Iran's parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted that "Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message", while Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said anyone expecting a shift in US policy towards Iran is "seriously mistaken" ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/iran-hails-us-voters-rejecting-war-while-khamenei-warns-hostility-wont-end)).
cards.why_it_matters: Democrats may try to restrict funding for the war, according to Andy Lipow, and oil traders read the result as raising the chance of a deal ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/oil-price-iran-war-us-election-strait-hormuz.html)). Trump also told the Financial Times the US is "locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it" ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/iran-hails-us-voters-rejecting-war-while-khamenei-warns-hostility-wont-end)).
cards.market_reaction: Oil fell 8.7% (CNBC); see the oil card.
cards.what_to_watch: Any statement from Washington or Tehran on talks, and any move in Congress to restrict war funding.

competing_views.view: Said the result is leading the market to conclude that Trump "might now be inclined to make a deal".
Said Trump is unlikely to walk away from preventing an Iranian nuclear weapon after paying "a huge price" for it.

close.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · after the close
summary: The ASX 200 rose 2.5% to 9,058.5, its biggest gain since 12 June according to Market Index, after Democrats won both houses of Congress. Tech rose 9.7% as NextDC jumped 48% on a stake build by Goodman and Digital Realty, and materials rose 7.3%; energy fell 4.4% and NAB 4.9% after its full-year result ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-thursday-5th-november); [ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-05/asx-markets-business-live-news-november-5-2026/107347286)).

Australia's goods trade surplus widened to A$2.83 billion in September from A$184 million in August, as gold imports fell (ABS). The Australian dollar was at US$0.7016, and a model based on ASX futures put the chance of a December RBA rise at 13.4% ([ABS](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/economy/international-trade/international-trade-goods/latest-release); [RBA Rate Watch](https://rbaratewatch.com/)).

Hong Kong rose 2.9% while Korea's KOSPI fell 4.9% on a chip sell-off. Brent futures eased 0.8% to US$93.84 after Wednesday's 8.7% fall, and the Bank of England decides at 11pm Sydney time, with a rise to 4% expected in a Reuters poll ([Investing.com](https://ph.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/asia-stocks-mixed-as-chip-rout-triggers-kospi-trading-halt-china-outperforms-2677035); [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/oil-falls-for-a-fourth-day-on-expectations-for-lower-risk-of-iran-war-escalation.html)).

cards.headline: ASX 200 rises 2.5% as tech and miners lead after US midterms
cards.takeaway: Eight of 11 sectors rose; energy, utilities and financials fell.
cards.new_since_last_issue: This morning's briefing had futures pointing to a rise of about 173 points; the index closed 224 points higher. Correction to Wednesday's Close tab, which gave 8,820.0 (−0.75%) from a 3:59pm read; the official close after the auction was 8,834.5 (−0.59%).
cards.what_happened: The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 9,058.5, up 224.0 points or 2.54% (close snapshot; Yahoo Finance), and the All Ordinaries rose 2.7%. Info tech rose 9.7%, materials 7.3%, health care 3.8%, property 3.0%, staples 2.9%, discretionary 2.8%, telecoms 2.2% and industrials 2.1%. Energy fell 4.4%, utilities 1.2% and financials 0.3% (S&P/ASX sector indices, Yahoo Finance, about 4:03pm). Market Index reported the session as the index's best since 12 June ([Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/asx-200-live-today-thursday-5th-november)).
cards.why_it_matters: Market Index linked the rally to the Democrats' win in both chambers of Congress, and said miners gained as copper and iron ore rebounded and gold miners followed bullion higher on a weaker US dollar. BHP rose 5.8%, Rio Tinto 7.1%, Fortescue 8.4%, Northern Star 9.2% and Evolution 13.2% (Yahoo Finance closing prices). Investing.com also pointed to the trade data released at 11:30am.
cards.what_to_watch: The Bank of England decision at 11pm, US payrolls at 12:30am Saturday and Macquarie's half-year result on Friday.

cards.headline: NextDC jumps 48% on a stake build; NAB falls 4.9% after its result
cards.takeaway: Company news drove the biggest moves at both ends of the index.
cards.what_happened: NextDC closed at A$9.67, up 48.1% (Yahoo Finance). It told the ASX that Ackland Investments, owned by Goodman Group and Digital Realty, ran an aftermarket bookbuild at A$9.50 a share for up to 9.9% of the company, and that "the board is not in possession of any takeover proposal at this time" ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-05/asx-markets-business-live-news-november-5-2026/107347286)). Goodman rose 5.7%. NAB closed down 4.9% at A$39.14, after trading as low as about A$38.02 (−7.7%) in the morning (Market Index). Its cash earnings fell 13% to A$6.1 billion, including a A$1.3 billion software amortisation charge; excluding that charge they were flat at A$7.1 billion, impairment charges rose 86% to A$1.55 billion and the full-year dividend was held at A$1.70 ([NAB](https://www.nab.com.au/news/nab-updates/nab-announces-its-2026-full-year-results); [Market Index](https://www.marketindex.com.au/news/nab-fy26-result-shares-head-for-worst-day-since-february-2025-as-bad-debts-nearly-double)). Eagers Automotive fell 12.8% after a trading update citing interest rates, inflation and fuel costs as pressures on industry margins ([Kalkine](https://kalkine.com.au/stock-analysis/retail/eagers-automotive-asxape-shares-slide-as-trading-update-flags-industry-headwinds)). Amcor fell 7.2% after its September-quarter adjusted EPS of US$0.95 was below the consensus figure cited by ChartMill ([Amcor](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/amcor-reports-solid-results-for-quarter-ended-september-30-2026-302929691.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Woodside fell 5.4% and Santos 5.2% with lower oil prices. At its capital markets day Woodside said it would cut at least 500 jobs, about 10% of its workforce, to reduce costs by A$550 million a year from 2028 ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-05/woodside-energy-to-slash-more-than-500-jobs/107349938)). Separately, David Jones entered voluntary administration with stores still trading, and Charter Hall Long WALE (owner of half its Elizabeth Street building) said its guidance was unchanged (ABC).

competing_views.view: Expect the cash rate to stay at 4.85% "for a while" and unemployment to reach about 5.5% by early 2028.

cards.headline: Hong Kong rises 2.9% while Korea falls 4.9% on a chip sell-off
cards.takeaway: Chipmakers fell in Seoul and Tokyo but rose in China after a PBoC rate cut on a buy-back facility.
cards.what_happened: At about 4:05pm Sydney time the KOSPI was down 4.9% at 5,403.3, the Nikkei down 1.6% at 61,181.4, the Shanghai Composite down 0.3% at 3,675.3 and the Hang Seng up 2.9% at 24,611.8 (close snapshot; Hong Kong trades until 7pm Sydney time). The KOSPI fell as much as 5.2% earlier, triggering a five-minute sell-side curb, as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell after weak results from Qualcomm and Arm ([Investing.com](https://ph.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/asia-stocks-mixed-as-chip-rout-triggers-kospi-trading-halt-china-outperforms-2677035)).
cards.why_it_matters: Investing.com reported that Chinese chip stocks rose after the People's Bank of China cut the rate on its relending facility for share buy-backs by 25bp to 1%. In Tokyo, Advantest and Tokyo Electron fell while the broader Topix rose in the morning session.

cards.headline: Trade surplus widens to A$2.83 billion; Australian dollar near US$0.70
cards.takeaway: Lower gold imports drove the larger surplus, and RBA December pricing barely moved.
cards.what_happened: The seasonally adjusted goods surplus rose to A$2.826 billion in September from A$184 million in August. Exports rose 2.3% and imports fell 3.3%, led by lower imports of non-monetary gold and civil aircraft ([ABS](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/economy/international-trade/international-trade-goods/latest-release)). Investing.com said economists had expected about A$940 million. The Australian dollar was at US$0.7016, up 0.7% (close snapshot, 4:21pm). MarketScreener's delayed quote had the 10-year yield near 5.02% at 4pm.
cards.why_it_matters: RBA Rate Watch, modelling ASX futures, put the chance of a December rise at 13.4%, down 1.4 points from 4 November, with a hold at 77.5% and a cut at 9.1%, as at 2:30pm. NAB's economists expect the cash rate to stay at 4.85% for a while (Market Index).

cards.headline: Brent eases to US$93.84 for a fourth fall; gold futures up 1.7%
cards.takeaway: Oil extended Wednesday's 8.7% drop while gold held above US$4,100.
cards.what_happened: Brent futures were at US$93.84, down 0.8%, gold futures at US$4,142.6, up 1.7%, and copper futures at US$6.41 a pound, up 0.2% (close snapshot, about 4:10pm). Iron ore was US$91.95 a tonne at Wednesday's close, up 1.0%. Brent and WTI both settled on Wednesday at their lowest since 31 August ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/oil-falls-for-a-fourth-day-on-expectations-for-lower-risk-of-iran-war-escalation.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: CNBC, citing Reuters, reported two sources close to Gulf government circles as saying a weakened Trump has more incentive to seek a deal with Iran, and JPMorgan estimated the oil market returned to a surplus of 1.4 million barrels a day in October as Gulf supply resumed.

competing_views.view: Does not expect prices to stay lower, noting the new Congress does not sit until January and commercial inventories are near 15-year lows.
Says markets are pricing a greater chance the war ends, but expects more volatility while the path to diplomacy is uncertain.

cards.headline: Bank of England decides at 11pm; US payrolls early Saturday
cards.takeaway: US index futures were mixed in Asian trade, with Nasdaq futures down about 1%.
cards.what_happened: At about 4:15pm Sydney time S&P 500 futures were down 0.2% and Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.1% (Yahoo Finance), after the S&P 500 rose 1.6% on Wednesday (close snapshot). The pound was at US$1.3493.
cards.why_it_matters: A Reuters poll expects the Bank of England to raise its rate to 4.00% from 3.75% at 11pm Sydney time, with a press conference at 11:30pm. US October payrolls are due at 12:30am Saturday, with economists polled by Reuters expecting 65,000 jobs.

cards.headline: Iran talks, David Jones' sale process and NextDC's register remain open
cards.takeaway: Each could produce new information in the coming days.
cards.what_happened: Reuters, via CNBC, reported Gulf-linked sources as seeing a full-scale US assault on Iran as less likely after the midterms, but no deal has been announced. David Jones' administrators, McGrathNicol, are running a sale or recapitalisation process with stores trading (ABC). NextDC's board said it holds no takeover proposal after Goodman and Digital Realty built their stake.
cards.why_it_matters: Oil prices, LNG producers and airlines remain sensitive to Iran headlines; property owners with David Jones leases, and data-centre peers, are exposed to the other two stories.
